dz.headerUnlocked: Unlocked. Destructive operations below are irreversible.
dz.headerLocked: Destructive maintenance operations. Requires the system owner credentials to enter.
dz.enterOwner: Enter the system owner credentials to open the reset console.
dz.notOwner: You do not have permission — this account is not the system owner.
dz.historianHelp: Pause to block all new time-series writes so the bucket stays empty after a wipe (e.g. for a clean demo). Reads/queries are unaffected. Resets to Active on API restart.
dz.resetProdDesc: Permanently deletes ALL production history from PostgreSQL: production orders, work orders, job orders, production events, batch records, material consumptions, scrap logs and reschedule requests — plus the derived KPI history that used to survive a reset: OEE records, machine state records, runtime hours, production snapshots, per-WO energy summaries and WO×machine energy ratios, traceability links and events, finished-goods lots and shift instances. Quality inspections, maintenance orders, downtime events and SPC measurements are preserved (their production links are cleared).
dz.resetProdDanger: all production orders, work orders, job orders and their data
dz.wipeTsDesc: Permanently deletes every point in the InfluxDB bucket "{{bucket}}" (OEE, energy, tag history). Note: a running edge gateway will repopulate live data immediately — stop it first to keep the bucket empty.
dz.willDelete: This will permanently delete {{danger}}. This action cannot be undone.
dz.alsoWipeTsDesc: Clears InfluxDB high-frequency production/OEE history in the same run.

toast.historianWipedDesc: All time-series points were deleted from InfluxDB.
toast.wipeFailedDesc: InfluxDB did not confirm the delete. Check the historian connection.
toast.historianPausedDesc: New time-series writes are blocked — the bucket stays empty.

dz.resetEnergyDesc: Permanently deletes energy meter readings, period summaries, per-WO energy summaries and WO×machine energy ratios from PostgreSQL. Meters, tariffs and device bindings are preserved. Kept separate from the production reset because these are real measurements streamed from physical meters — a running edge gateway will repopulate live data immediately, so stop it first to keep the tables empty.
dz.resetEnergyDanger: This permanently deletes all energy meter readings and every KPI derived from them. Measured history cannot be recovered.

downtime.title: Reset Downtime & Machine Timeline
downtime.desc: Deletes every downtime event and the machine state history behind it. The two are cleared together because they describe the same minutes from two angles — clearing one alone leaves OEE with a timeline that has no reasons. Downtime causes and categories are configuration and are preserved.
downtime.danger: all downtime events and machine state records

quality.title: Reset Quality Records
quality.desc: Deletes inspections, inspection results, non-conformances, CAPAs and SPC measurements. The quality catalogue — defect types, inspection plans, characteristics and control limits — is configuration somebody built and is preserved.
quality.danger: all quality inspections, NCRs, CAPAs and SPC measurements

maintenance.title: Reset Maintenance History
maintenance.desc: Deletes maintenance work orders and the PM tasks scheduled from a plan. Assets, preventive-maintenance plans and spare-part definitions are the maintenance plan, not its history, and are preserved.
maintenance.danger: all maintenance work orders and scheduled PM tasks

alarms.title: Reset Alarm History
alarms.desc: Deletes every recorded alarm event. Alarm rules — the conditions, thresholds, deadbands and delays — are configuration and are preserved, so alarms keep firing from the next reading onwards.

shifts.title: Reset Shift Instances & Planned Stops
shifts.desc: Deletes generated shift instances and the planned-stop events materialised from them. Shift templates, schedules and planned-stop definitions survive — they are how the plant is configured to run — so a fresh range can be materialised straight afterwards.
shifts.danger: all shift instances and materialised planned stops

inventory.title: Reset Inventory Movements
inventory.desc: Deletes the stock movement log. Items, warehouses, locations and current stock levels are master data and are preserved.

notifications.title: Reset Notifications
notifications.desc: Deletes the notification history that accumulates over a long demo. Nothing else is affected.

backups.title: Database Backups
backups.subtitle: Take a full copy of the database at any moment. Copies are stored on the server and can be restored, downloaded or deleted from here.
backups.empty: No backups yet. Take one before any reset.
backups.listFailed: Could not load the backup list.
backups.restoreDesc: This REPLACES the entire database with "{{label}}", taken {{when}}. Everything recorded since then is lost.
backups.safetyNote: A safety copy of the current database is taken automatically first, and its id is shown when the restore finishes — so this is reversible.
backups.restoredDesc: A safety copy was kept as {{id}}. The page will reload.
backups.deleteDesc: "{{label}}" will be removed from the server permanently. This does not affect the database itself.
backups.storageNote: Backups live on a persistent volume on the server, so they survive a container rebuild. Download the ones that matter — a copy that only exists on the same machine as the database is not an offsite backup.
backups.importHint: Upload a .dump archive from this computer so it can be restored from here. Only PostgreSQL custom-format archives (pg_dump -Fc) are accepted.
